items.title: Dink Johnson Interview, 1950-11-12
items.q: Well Dick, can you play any of Jelly's tunes?

ctx.x: Oh I was about nineteen. Where did you leave? How come you left? What made you get the edge? I left on account of my sister, she sent for me to come out here. She was living out here? Yeah. In L.A.? No, in Las Vegas. And she had a saloon man, she wanted me to come out and help her. Did you play piano on the saloon? Yeah I played piano in the tin bar in the daytime, played piano at night.

I was busy. Yeah, I was very busy. Well Dick, can you play any of Jelly's tunes? You don't have to worry about them. Things like, you know, Marlenburg or... Yep. No, I don't know that. Wolverine. Any of them that you know. Let's see. I'll play you this one. Hey, kids are like that. I know they will. Because they're going to hear you talking to them. Yeah. That's what I did. They'll go from there, I noticed that. How to build their dear Thank you.
Thank you. Thank you. Thank you.
